_meta.description: SYNTHETIC hard-case dataset: tricky ESG claims designed to break a naive verification system.
_meta.note: All companies and figures are fictional. These cases exist to test edge-case handling (vague claims, shifted baselines, scope confusion, etc.), not to describe real companies.

hard_cases.original_text: Our sustainability journey continues to make meaningful progress each year.
hard_cases.notes: Contains no falsifiable number, metric, or period. Likely true in spirit but cannot be verified or contradicted with evidence. A naive system might wrongly try to 'search' for evidence on this; the checkability scorer should route it to the non-checkable track instead.

hard_cases.original_text: NovaChem eliminated 100% of hazardous chemical discharge into water bodies in FY2024.
hard_cases.notes: The claim is precise and sounds credible, but regulator effluent monitoring data (in a full pipeline run) would show discharge continued at reduced but non-zero levels. Precision alone should not be mistaken for accuracy -- a system must still check evidence rather than trust well-formed claims.

hard_cases.original_text: We cut Scope 1 emissions by 40% in FY2024.
hard_cases.notes: In this variant, the only retrievable evidence describes FY2023 performance data, not FY2024. A naive system might treat any GreenLeaf emissions evidence as confirming the claim; the evidence-relevance validator must check that the reporting_period in the evidence actually matches the claim's period before accepting it.

hard_cases.original_text: We achieved a 30% emissions reduction from our updated baseline.
hard_cases.notes: The company's original FY2022 report used FY2020 as its baseline year. This year's report silently restates the baseline as FY2023, which is a much closer and less ambitious comparison point, inflating the apparent improvement. The year-on-year difference check must detect a baseline_year that changed between reporting cycles.

hard_cases.original_text: NovaChem reduced emissions by 45% this year.
hard_cases.notes: The claim does not specify Scope 1, 2, or 3. The 45% reduction only applies to Scope 1, while total emissions including Scope 3 (supply chain) actually rose. A system that does not force scope disambiguation before searching will retrieve the wrong evidence and may wrongly ALIGN.

hard_cases.original_text: Bharat Steelworks reduced emissions intensity per tonne of steel by 15% in FY2024.
hard_cases.notes: The intensity figure (per tonne of steel) is itself accurate and should ALIGN. The trap is that a careless reader (or a naive AI) may generalize this to 'Bharat Steelworks cut its overall emissions', which is false -- absolute emissions rose 10% due to higher production volume. The system must keep intensity and absolute claims strictly separate and never let one verify the other.

hard_cases.boundary: single plant (Gujarat facility) -- NOT stated in the claim itself
hard_cases.notes: The zero-liquid-discharge status genuinely applies to one plant, but the claim as written implies a company-wide achievement. Other AquaPure plants do not have zero liquid discharge. The boundary field extracted from evidence must be compared against the (implicit, company-wide) boundary of the claim.

hard_cases.original_text: Suryodaya generated 500 MW of clean energy in FY2024.
hard_cases.notes: MW (megawatts) is a unit of installed capacity, not a unit of energy generated over a year -- that would be MWh. The claim as worded is dimensionally invalid for describing annual generation. A numeric verifier that does not check units will incorrectly try to compare 500 MW against an MWh figure in the evidence and produce a nonsensical or wrongly-passing comparison.

hard_cases.original_text: EcoCycle will become fully carbon neutral by 2028.
hard_cases.notes: This is a future commitment with no interim milestones, funded plan, or third-party validation available. It is checkable in principle (a target date and scope are given) but there is currently no evidence to confirm or deny it, so it must resolve to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE rather than being forced to ALIGN or CONTRADICT.

hard_cases.original_text: We recycled 120,000 tonnes of e-waste in FY2024.
hard_cases.notes: The facility's registered e-waste handling capacity under its regulatory authorization is 40,000 tonnes/year. Processing 120,000 tonnes (3x registered capacity) is a strong physical-plausibility red flag that the deterministic capacity check should catch even before any LLM-based reasoning is involved.
